newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-SPONSOR PULL OUT AFTER MASS BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-SPONSOR PULL OUT AFTER MASS BRAWL.

text.p: The future of rugby league in Australia suffered a blow on Tuesday when a major sponsor withdrew its support for a national schoolboy competition in reaction to a vicious brawl in a televised match.
The Commonwealth Bank, Australia's second largest bank, ended its 17-year sponsorship after two Brisbane teams became involved in an on-field mass brawl last week.
Twelve players from one school have been suspended for periods ranging from one week to 12 months. The other school has yet to discipline its players.
"The bank does not condone violent behaviour and found this most recent incident totally unacceptable," Commonwealth Bank spokesman Alf Long said in a statement on Tuesday.
Australian Rugby League, which organises the schoolboy competition, accused the bank of losing its sense of priority by ending its sponsorship.
The loss of the A$100,000 (US$78,000) a year deal is a setback for a sport already bitterly divided by media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's creation of a breakaway league in Australia.
Murdoch's Super League was launched this season in competition with the existing Australian Rugby League premiership.
